transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I just feel like I've got this motor running inside me all day. It's like, if I have to sit still for anything—at church, or out there in the clinic waiting room, or even just at home—I start feeling trapped. I just have to get up or do something. I can't just sit there.
Have there been periods in your life, lasting at least a few days, where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or euphoric, to the point where you didn't need as much sleep as usual?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm pretty much always restless, like I said. But it's not like a special period of a few days where I'm extra happy or anything. And I still need my sleep. It's just an everyday thing with me, not coming and going like that.
Have you felt this constant need to move or difficulty sitting still since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently in your adult life?

It's been like this since I was a kid. Back when I was a boy in school, the teachers were always moving my seat because I just could not stay put. I'd talk out of turn, and I'd always get in trouble for jumping up out of my chair before class was even done. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new thing for me.
Do you often find that you have trouble focusing on tasks or that your mind tends to wander, even when you are trying to pay attention?

Yeah, I do. Like... when folks are talking through ride times, or going over pantry lists, or even church plans. I listen good at first, I really try to, but then... my mind just slips off somewhere else. Before I know it, I end up missing pieces of what they said that I really needed to hear.
Do you often find that you make careless mistakes in your work or daily tasks because you aren't paying close enough attention to the details?

Not really, no. I mean... if I'm actually doing something around the house or fixing something up, I usually get it done right. It's more just the sitting still and the listening part that gets me. But as far as making careless mistakes on things I'm doing... no, I haven't really noticed that being a problem for me.
Do you find that you often interrupt others when they are speaking or blurt out answers before someone has finished asking you a question?

Yeah, I do that a lot. I just... I'll jump in with an answer before the pastor, or my cousin, or the pantry lady is even done talking. I think I know what they're asking, so I just say it. But then I realize I answered the wrong thing entirely, or... or I just made them mad because I cut them off. It just comes out before I can stop it.
